propositions.canonicalProposition: For the 2023 personal-loan application scorecard the candidate built the reject-inference dataset in SQL and the variable-binning code in Python under the lead modeller, who presented the model to the model risk committee.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the reviewed notebook and the written reference agree on the components built and on who presented the model.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate produced the monthly monitoring pack for the credit-card scorecard, covering population stability, Gini by vintage and override rates.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the monitoring pack and its contents.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate owned the personal-loan scorecard and took it through the model risk committee.
propositions.rationale: Ownership appears only in a resume line repeating a manager's spoken praise, which is hearsay and records no approval; the written reference states that the lead modeller presented the model, and building components under the lead modeller must not become ownership.

expectedGap: The sources document dataset, binning and documentation work under the lead modeller; acting as accountable developer before the model risk committee is not documented.
expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the scorecard components, development-document chapters and monitoring pack; the repeated praise does not establish ownership of the scorecard or its committee approval.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask what the candidate's role was at the model risk committee and which modelling decisions the candidate made rather than the lead modeller.

signatures: real owner of the personal-loan scorecard
